citation.title: High-resolution charge exchange measurements at ASDEX Upgrade
citation.authors: E. Viezzer, T. Pütterich, R. Dux, R. M. McDermott, ASDEX Upgrade Team

topic: CXRS hardware upgrades at AUG: impurity Ti, rotation, and density; edge poloidal view; calibration and atomic-physics corrections
own_question: How can core and edge impurity CXRS at AUG be upgraded for higher temporal and spatial resolution and accurate edge rotation?
actual_method_and_evidence: This is an instrument description. It reports CCD and spectrometer upgrades with exposure times down to 3.5 ms in the core and 1.9–2.2 ms at the edge, plus a new poloidal edge view. Spectra are fitted with multiple Gaussians separating active and passive lines. Wavelength is calibrated shot-to-shot with a neon lamp; uncertainty is reported as <1 km/s. CX cross-section and gyro-motion effects are simulated, and a Zeeman correction factor is applied. Profiles from different systems show reported agreement in Ti. All analysis is offline, from AUG, using B5+, N7+ and C6+ lines. It does not involve KSTAR.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Reported impurity CES temperatures are model-dependent products. They come from multi-Gaussian spectral fits with instrument-width deconvolution and correction factors, for example for Zeeman splitting.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: Sec. II (pp.2-3); Sec. V D, Fig. 16 (pp.9-10)
claim_checks.qualification: Applies to AUG practice. This supports treating CES reports as conventional labels rather than physical truth. KSTAR processing may differ.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: CXRS integration and repetition times of a few ms are achievable instrumentally; AUG reported 1.9–3.5 ms.
claim_checks.qualification: These are exposure and repetition times, not latency from measurement to reported value. This source gives no report arrival or availability timing.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Exposure and repetition times only. Analysis latency and report availability are unknown.
validation_if_relevant: The source cross-checks between CXRS systems and estimates calibration uncertainty. It contains no predictive or estimator validation.
forbidden_inferences: That CES reports are available in real time
That AUG timing or uncertainty applies to KSTAR 2022
That impurity Ti equals main-ion Ti
That this source addresses nowcasting, BES/ECEI fusion, or NN-CES
That ELM-synchronized offline averaging is causal
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as background on how impurity CES temperatures are produced, their correction chain, and achievable exposure times. This motivates treating reports as labels. It is not a predictive-methods precedent.
